= sqlparser changes for RTDB

This is sqlparser 0.63.0 from crates.io, under the Apache License 2.0 in LICENSE.TXT.
The published archive has SHA-256 `3679862809bd1f92e563cf6fd820e28f39135303668001c10331d5027183e8b4`.

RTDB's dialect enables the FROM-first query specification from the XTDB grammar.
The parser records each WHERE and SELECT tail in source order, including GROUP BY and HAVING before the SELECT they belong to.
The syntax tree retains the usual expression nodes and their spans, and the existing set-operation parser consumes each FROM-first specification as one operand.
The flag defaults to false, preserving the upstream dialects' FROM-first syntax.

RTDB's dialect recognizes VALUES as a subquery prefix in the same parser decision as SELECT and WITH.
The parsed scalar and quantified subqueries retain the original VALUES body and token locations.

RTDB's dialect parses USER through the ordinary identifier expression grammar.
The binder resolves its column reference and session value using the active scope.

RTDB's dialect retains expressions used as table sources in expression-derived table nodes.
These nodes retain the expression, optional ordinality, and alias.

RTDB's admitted SQL batch parser and statement splitter use the tokenizer's boundary mode to emit comment tokens with empty text fields.
Each ordinary line or block comment occupies one token with its original location and participates in the same buffer growth.
Block comments retain their dialect-specific nesting and end-of-input diagnostics.
Full SQL tokenization retains original comment text.
Dialect-enabled optimizer hints still expand, preserving text in any comment tokens they emit.

RTDB preserves doubled double-quote and backtick delimiters when the tokenizer reads a quoted identifier.
String literals use the dialect's existing unescape rules.

The RTDB dialect disables dedicated `TABLE(expr)` parsing in table-factor position.
`TABLE` then follows ordinary identifier and function-expression parsing.

`VALUES` rows retain either a scalar expression or a row constructor in the AST.
The RTDB dialect accepts both forms and allows empty row constructors.

RTDB's dialect parses `RECORDS` followed by `{` or a placeholder as a query body holding one expression per row.
The same prefix starts a statement and a parenthesized subquery, so an unquoted `records` column reference still parses as an identifier.

RTDB's dialect reads an optional `ALL` or `DISTINCT` after `GROUP BY` as the SQL:2011 set quantifier and drops it, so grouping elements must follow.
`GROUP BY ALL` without grouping elements is a syntax error rather than the dialect-specific group-by-all form.
